prompt: Suppose $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = 4$ and $\lim_{x \to a} g(x) = -2$. Find $\lim_{x \to a} \left[ 3f(x) - g(x) \right]$.
hint: Limits respect constant multiples, sums and differences, so you may take the limit of each piece separately.

hints.text: Limits respect constant multiples, sums and differences, so you may take the limit of each piece separately.
The constant multiple law gives $\lim 3f(x) = 3 \cdot 4 = 12$, and you know $\lim g(x) = -2$. Now subtract the second from the first, watching the signs.
Subtracting a negative adds: $12 - (-2) = 14$, so the limit is $14$.

explanation: By the constant multiple law, the $3$ can come outside: $\lim 3f(x) = 3 \lim f(x) = 3 \cdot 4 = 12$.
By the difference law, the limit of a difference is the difference of the limits: $\lim [3f(x) - g(x)] = 12 - (-2)$.
Subtracting $-2$ is the same as adding $2$, so the limit is $14$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pretend they are numbers
steps: Near $x = a$, $f(x)$ behaves like $4$ and $g(x)$ behaves like $-2$.
That is $14$. The limit laws say this shortcut is legitimate.
